subject: Numeracy
title: Sorting by size and kind
objectives: Children will sort objects by size into big and small groups.
Children will sort objects by kind and give a one-word reason with support.
content: Sorting objects by size and by kind, with a simple reason such as "because they are fruits".
teachingActivities: Think aloud as you sort; ask "Why does it go here?"; offer the sentence "because it is a fruit" and accept gestures.
learnerActivities: Sort big and small objects, sort fruits from toys and clothes, and give a one-word or gesture reason.
resources: Big and small spoons, cups and balls
Toy or large real fruits (oranges, mango)
assessment: Check that each child can sort by size and by kind and note any reasons they give.
expectedOutcomes: Sorts by size or by kind with growing accuracy.
Offers a word or gesture as a reason.
crossCurricular: Science: living and non-living, fruit and food
Social Habits: tidying into the right basket

lessons.title: Big things, small things
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sort objects into a big group and a small group.
successCriteria: Places a big object with the big group
Places a small object with the small group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour with support and use some size words.
resources: Two baskets labelled BIG and SMALL with pictures
Eight pairs of big and small objects (spoons, cups, balls, blocks)
lessons.starter: Hold up a big spoon and a small spoon. Ask "Which one goes in the big basket?" and "Which one goes in the small basket?"
teacherActivities: Sort a few objects while thinking aloud: "A big ball. Big basket."
Hand a child an object and ask "Is it big or small?" before they place it.
Mix up the objects and sort again as a group, one child at a time.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say "big" with you.
Child decides and places it in the right basket.
Each child sorts one object and others check by pointing.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sort a few objects while thinking aloud: "A big ball. Big basket." Children: Children watch and say "big" with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Hand a child an object and ask "Is it big or small?" before they place it. Children: Child decides and places it in the right basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Mix up the objects and sort again as a group, one child at a time. Children: Each child sorts one object and others check by pointing.

practical.title: Big and small baskets
steps: Spread the mixed objects on the mat.
Children sort them into the two baskets.
Teacher and children look at each basket and say "big" or "small".
practical.safety: Use objects that are larger than a child’s fist. Supervise to keep objects out of mouths.

differentiation.support: Offer one object at a time with clear size contrast.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose a medium-sized object and decide which basket it fits best.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is this spoon big or small?
Which basket does the small ball go in?

lessons.conclusion: Look at the two baskets and say "Big things, small things." Tidy together.
lessons.homeConnection: Sort cups and plates into big and small piles at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort objects into a big group and a small group" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Fruits and toys
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sort fruits and toys into two groups.
successCriteria: Puts fruits in the fruit basket
Puts toys in the toy basket
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour with support and use some size words.
resources: Toy or large safe fruits (orange, mango, banana)
lessons.starter: Hold up a mango and a toy car. Say "This is a fruit. This is a toy. They are different kinds."
teacherActivities: Sort four objects aloud: "Mango, fruit. Car, toy."
Let each child pick an object and say whether it is a fruit or a toy.
Ask "Why is the orange in the fruit basket?" and give the sentence "because it is a fruit".
learnerActivities: Child places it in the correct basket.
Child says "fruit" or points to the fruit picture.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sort four objects aloud: "Mango, fruit. Car, toy." Children: Children repeat "fruit" and "toy".
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child pick an object and say whether it is a fruit or a toy. Children: Child places it in the correct basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Why is the orange in the fruit basket?" and give the sentence "because it is a fruit". Children: Child says "fruit" or points to the fruit picture.

practical.title: Fruit and toy basket
practical.safety: Real fruit must be washed and not eaten unless offered as a snack. Use only large toys that cannot be swallowed.

differentiation.support: Use two very different objects such as a ball and a banana.
differentiation.extension: Introduce a third group, clothes, and sort three kinds.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is this a fruit or a toy?
Why does it go in this basket?
questions.expected: A word or gesture such as "fruit".

expectedOutcomes: Gives a one-word reason with support
lessons.conclusion: Sing "Fruits in the basket, toys on the shelf." Tidy up.
lessons.homeConnection: Sort fruit and vegetables or toys and clothes at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort fruits and toys into two groups" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Clothes, food and toys
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sort objects into three kinds: clothes, food and toys.
successCriteria: Says or points to the kind
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour with support and use some size words.
resources: Three baskets labelled clothes, food and toys
Objects: sock, hat, orange, plantain, ball, block
lessons.starter: Hold a sock, an orange and a ball. Say "Which one do we wear? Which one do we eat? Which one do we play with?"
teacherActivities: Sort three objects aloud using "we wear, we eat, we play".
Hand out objects and ask "Where does it go?"
Ask "How do you know?" Wait and accept gestures.
learnerActivities: Children repeat the phrases and gestures.
Child places it in the right basket.
Child shows eating, wearing or playing.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sort three objects aloud using "we wear, we eat, we play". Children: Children repeat the phrases and gestures.
Step 2. Teacher: Hand out objects and ask "Where does it go?" Children: Child places it in the right basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "How do you know?" Wait and accept gestures. Children: Child shows eating, wearing or playing.

practical.title: Wear, eat, play sort
steps: Place the baskets in a row.
Children take an object and act out what it does.
They place it in the matching basket.
practical.safety: Real food must be fresh, washed and eaten only when the teacher offers it. Use clean clothes.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to think of another thing that goes in each basket.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Do we wear it, eat it or play with it?
Which basket does the hat go in?

lessons.conclusion: Sing "We wear, we eat, we play." Tidy up the baskets.
lessons.homeConnection: At bedtime, sort clean clothes and toys into different places.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort objects into three kinds: clothes, food and toys" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Because they are fruits
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will give a simple reason for how they sorted.
successCriteria: Says or shows why an object goes in a group
Uses a word like "fruit" or a gesture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour with support and use some size words.
resources: Picture cards for reasons (apple, shirt, ball)
lessons.starter: Say "A magic bag! Let us sort what comes out. Then I will ask you why."
teacherActivities: Pull an object from the bag and sort it with a reason: "It goes here because it is a fruit."
Let each child pull an object, decide where it goes and say why.
learnerActivities: Children repeat "because it is a fruit".
Child sorts and gives a word or gesture.
Child names or finds another object.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pull an object from the bag and sort it with a reason: "It goes here because it is a fruit." Children: Children repeat "because it is a fruit".
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child pull an object, decide where it goes and say why. Children: Child sorts and gives a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What else goes here?" Children: Child names or finds another object.

practical.title: Magic bag sorting
steps: Put objects in a cloth bag.
Each child takes one and places it in the right basket.
practical.safety: Keep objects safe and large. Supervise to avoid mouthing.

differentiation.support: Offer picture cards for the child to point to as a reason.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to think of a new kind, such as animals, and sort.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Why does the orange go here?
What else goes in this basket?

lessons.conclusion: Clap a rhythm for each sorted basket. Say "Because, because!"
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child why they put things together when tidying.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "give a simple reason for how they sorted" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sorting stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sort by size and kind at three stations.
successCriteria: Sorts correctly by size and kind
Offers a word or gesture as a reason
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can sort by colour with support and use some size words.
lessons.starter: Sing "Big and small, fruits and toys" and show the stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask observed children to sort and say why.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child sorts and gives a reason.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children sort at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask observed children to sort and say why. Children: Child sorts and gives a reason.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Remove small items and supervise all stations.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner at each station.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a friend through sorting.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: sorts by size; sorts by kind; gives a reason.

questions.question: Why did you put it there?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
lessons.conclusion: Sing the sorting song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child sort objects around the house this week.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort by size and kind at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
